title: A Prom for the Group Chat
premise: Noor Ishikawa, a scholarship student at Halcyon Academy, is dragged into a mysterious group chat that predicts events before they happen — including her own death on the night of prom. The chat is a dying experiment left by the academy's founder, feeding on a 'championship' of choices: the public fencing tournament everyone watches, and a hidden inheritance trial that decides who controls the school's future. As Noor races through both competitions, she learns the chat's other members are all candidates, and one of them will do anything to survive. In the end, Noor wins the trial not by defeating her rivals but by refusing the founder's terms, breaking the chat's predictive grip — and she survives prom, choosing her own future over the inheritance.
about_author: Jude Fairweather is a former debate coach who writes young adult fiction about overachievers unraveling beautifully. They live near the coast with an unreasonable number of houseplants and a group chat that has never once predicted the future.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She navigates Halcyon Academy's glittering halls on scholarship, keeping her head down and her fencing stats up. A late-night study session establishes her best friend Priya, her crush on rival fencer Elias, and the crushing weight of needing the end-of-year championship stipend. Beat: fragile normalcy, one breath before the fall.

chapters.title: Unknown Number, Unknown Members
chapters.summary: Noor is added to a group chat called 'Halcyon Futures' by an unknown admin. The members: Priya, Elias, and three strangers. The first message predicts tomorrow's fire drill to the minute. It happens. Noor's POV; the beat is a chill of curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Second Prediction
chapters.summary: The chat predicts a teacher's resignation and a flooded gym — both come true. Noor tries to leave the chat; the exit button doesn't work. Elias messages her privately, scared, asking if she's in it too. His POV closes the chapter, revealing he received a warning about Noor specifically. Beat: the trap tightens.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: The admin finally speaks: the chat exists to choose an heir to Halcyon's founder. The six members are candidates. The 'championship' is twofold — the public fencing tournament and a hidden trial. Refusal means expulsion and the loss of Noor's scholarship. Noor's POV; beat: fury at being conscripted, and the first hint that the chat punishes disobedience.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Something
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She's been in the chat longest and has been quietly researching the founder, Marguerite Halcyon, whose death in 1987 is suspiciously undocumented. Priya hides her findings from Noor to protect her. Beat: love expressed as secrecy, the friendship's first hairline crack.

chapters.title: First Bout
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Tournament qualifiers begin; Noor faces one of the stranger candidates, Wren, who fences with impossible foresight — as if she already knows Noor's moves. Noor loses narrowly. Beat: humiliation, and the terrifying realization the chat's predictions can be weaponized.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Following a chat riddle, he finds a sealed sub-basement archive with Marguerite's journals. He learns the 'trial' has killed candidates before — the founder's machine trades futures for predictions. He tells Noor everything except the part that names her. Beat: dread, and a first real moment of intimacy between them.

chapters.title: What the Chat Wants
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The chat escalates: a prediction names Priya's scholarship as forfeit unless Noor wins her next match. Noor realizes the chat manufactures the crises it predicts. She trains obsessively, pushing Elias away. Beat: isolation as sacrifice, love against duty sharpening.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reveals she was a candidate last cycle; her brother took the inheritance and hasn't been seen since. She's not Noor's enemy — she's proof of the stakes. She warns Noor: the final candidate standing inherits the machine, and the machine eats its heir. Beat: enemy becomes reluctant ally.

chapters.title: Semifinals
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She wins the semifinal against Elias in a brutal, heartbreaking bout — the chat predicted the winner, and Noor fights to prove it wrong, then realizes she fought to the exact predicted score. Beat: the horror of free will dissolving; Elias's quiet pride and hurt.

chapters.title: The Missing Day
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers a gap in the school records: a full day in 1987 erased. In the archive she finds the founder's final entry — the machine was built to save Marguerite's dying daughter, and it failed, and it has been searching for a replacement ever since. Beat: grief at the heart of the horror.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Chat
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A candidate, Marcus, leaks Noor's scholarship status to the whole school, framing it as chat 'transparency.' Humiliated and suspended from practice, Noor hits bottom — until Elias publicly defends her at cost to his own standing. Beat: public ruin, private tenderness.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: The six candidates are summoned at midnight to the sub-basement. The trial is revealed: three tasks testing judgment, sacrifice, and desire. The first task forces each candidate to reveal their deepest secret to the chat. Noor's POV; beat: exposure, and the strange relief of being fully seen.

chapters.title: Sacrifice
chapters.summary: The second task demands each candidate give up something irreplaceable. Priya forfeits her spot — and her memories of the chat — to shield Noor. Noor watches her best friend look at her like a stranger. Priya's POV for the final scene, from inside the forgetting. Beat: the price of survival, paid by someone you love.

chapters.title: Desire
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The final task shows each candidate the future they want most. Noor sees prom, Elias, a scholarship won honestly, Priya laughing. The machine offers it all — if she accepts the inheritance. She feels the pull and understands why candidates vanish. Beat: temptation rendered tender, the cruelest test yet.

chapters.title: What Elias Chose
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He accepted a lesser version of the deal years ago — his family's debts cleared — and the chat has held his leash since. He confesses everything to Noor, expecting her to hate him. Instead she asks him to prom, properly, mid-ruin. Beat: honesty as the only winning move; love chosen over leverage.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The public fencing final, against Wren, with the whole school watching. Noor fences brilliantly and deliberately loses — refusing to let the machine script her triumph. The crowd's disappointment is deafening. The chat goes silent, which is worse. Beat: defiance disguised as defeat.

chapters.title: Countdown to Prom
chapters.summary: The chat's final prediction arrives: 'NOOR ISHIKAWA DIES AT PROM, 11:47 PM.' Marcus, desperate to inherit, begins sabotaging the prom preparations to force the prophecy. Wren and Elias rally to Noor's defense. Noor's POV; beat: ticking-clock terror, allies assembled.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Gowns, music, a slow dance with Elias — all under a countdown. At 11:40, Marcus triggers the machine directly in the basement; the building's systems begin failing, the gym doors sealing. Noor realizes the prophecy isn't a threat — it's the machine's self-fulfilling design. Beat: beauty and dread braided together.

Climax. Noor descends into the machine room as the clock strikes the predicted minute. She confronts the machine — and Marcus, half-consumed by it. She refuses the inheritance, offers it nothing, and instead does the one thing no candidate tried: she forgives Marguerite, and walks away from the deal. The prediction breaks; the chat dies. Elias and Wren pull her out. Beat: the prophecy fails because she stops playing.

chapters.title: After
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The school reels from the 'gas leak.' Marcus survives, hollowed; Wren stays to search for her brother in what remains of the archive. Priya's memories return in fragments — the first one back is Noor's name. Beat: aftermath, grief, and the slow return of the people she loves.

chapters.title: A Prom for the Group Chat
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Noor's POV. Weeks later, the school throws the prom it never finished. Noor, scholarship intact on her own terms, dances with Elias while Priya films everything for a brand-new group chat — one that predicts absolutely nothing. Final beat: an ordinary future, chosen and unscripted, worth more than any inheritance.
